processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 15, 17, 19) ingots produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere; this sample is the 15Al alloy (Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 at.%).
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching; this is the parent process (proc_st-1100c-10min-oq) of the sample.
Solution-treated 15Al sample aged at 600 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching (terminal state of process proc_aging-600c-3h).

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 15Al alloy at 600 °C and above, the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within just 1 h; abundant fine precipitates, identified (with EBSD) as BCC and FCC phases, were present within the β-Mn.

phases_present.morphology: Dominant near-complete matrix after the α→β-Mn transformation; β-Mn generally precipitates as short rod-shaped phase along α grain boundaries and inside α grains, growing until precipitates contact one another.
Fine precipitates rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn, slightly poor in Al

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The FCC Cu-rich and BCC phases at the β-Mn interfaces were characterized by TEM (Figs. 11 and 12) and EBSD (Figs. 4, 5, 6) on the peak-hardness Fe-Mn-Al-Cu samples; the same interface precipitation is reported generically for the ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys (b0068, b0052). No interface characterization was performed specifically at the 600 °C/3 h condition.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness, load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the hardness values given as the average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the hardness value given by the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 600 °C for 3 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Al aged at 600 °C for 3 h exhibits a Vickers hardness of 938.2 ± 18.0 HV (Table 2).

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 3 h, the only condition-specific quantitative datum reported is the Vickers hardness (938.2 ± 18.0 HV, Table 2); no EBSD/SEM/TEM micrograph panel exists for this exact condition — the 15Al characterizations were performed at 525 °C/3 h, 550 °C/6 h and 650 °C/3 h (EBSD Fig. 4), the SEM matrix of Fig. 7 covers 525/550/575 °C (1,3,6,10 h) plus 600 °C-1 h, 600 °C-6 h, 625 °C-1 h and 650 °C-1 h, and the TEM study (Fig. 11) was on the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h (the peak-hardness 965.6 HV condition).

For the 15Al alloy, the optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness was reported as mainly 525 °C–600 °C, and the aging-hardening kinetic/structural trends at 600 °C and above (near-complete α→β-Mn transformation within ~1 h with fine BCC and FCC precipitates) are the general context within which the 600 °C/3 h state sits; the samples' peak hardness 965.6 HV is reached at 600 °C/6 h (a different aging condition / sibling sample).
